summary: Splendor is a light engine-building game where players collect gem tokens to buy development cards, which in turn provide permanent discounts that snowball toward richer purchases and noble visits. It plays in about half an hour and is often a gateway game for new players.
praised: extremely quick to teach and play
satisfying engine snowball as discounts compound
portable and reliably enjoyable as a filler
criticised: limited direct interaction beyond taking chips or sniping a card someone wants
can feel a bit solitaire once you're deep in your own plan
luck of the card flip affects available options

interaction.detail: Players draw chips from a common supply and buy or reserve cards from a shared row of development cards, so taking a card or the last of a gem color denies it to opponents. Each player's tableau of owned cards is otherwise built and scored individually.

scoring.how_you_win: Collect gem chips to buy development cards that generate prestige points and permanent discounts; the round after a player reaches 15 points is completed and whoever has the most points wins.
scoring.score_note: game ends once someone hits 15, but the round finishes so final total often runs a bit higher
